messages.text: Leclerc seals Mexico City practice double as Hamilton suffers technical issue

metadata.summary: Charles Leclerc completed a Friday practice double at the Mexico City Grand Prix but Ferrari's strong showing was dampened by Lewis Hamilton suffering a technical issue.
metadata.content: Mexico City GP: Charles Leclerc completes Friday practice double as Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton suffers technical failure | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Mexico City GP: Charles Leclerc completes Friday practice double as Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton suffers technical failure Charles Leclerc tops both Friday practice sessions for Ferrari; Lewis Hamilton suffers technical failure; Max Verstappen collides with Liam Lawson; watch every Mexico City GP session live on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 9pm on Saturday and the race at 8pm on Sunday Friday 30 October 2026 23:34, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Friday's practice sessions at the Mexico City Grand Prix Charles Leclerc completed a Friday practice double at the Mexico City Grand Prix but Ferrari's strong showing was dampened by Lewis Hamilton suffering a technical issue. Leclerc produced a time of 1:17.827s to finish just over a tenth clear of McLaren's Lando Norris and Mercedes' George Russell, with the British pair among 10 drivers who had earlier sat out the opening session to make way for rookie drivers. Kimi Antonelli, who only needs to finish ninth in Sunday's race to become Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion, was a tenth down on his team-mate Russell in fourth. messages.text: Brilliant Sun Goddess in class of her own at Breeders' Cup

metadata.summary: Sun Goddess confirmed herself as a two-year-old out of the ordinary with a clear-cut win Breeders' Cup Juvenile Fillies Turf at Keeneland.
metadata.content: Breeders' Cup: Sun Goddess in class of her own with Juvenile Fillies Turf win at Keeneland as Libertango takes Juvenile Turf Sprint | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Breeders' Cup: Sun Goddess in class of her own with Juvenile Fillies Turf win at Keeneland as Libertango takes Juvenile Turf Sprint Sun Goddess capped off a memorable two-year-old season with a fourth success at the top level with a scintillating display in the Breeders' Cup Juvenile Fillies Turf on a winning night for the European raiders at Keeneland; Libertango won the opening Juvenile Turf Sprint Friday 30 October 2026 22:08, UK Image: Sun Goddess, ridden by Ryan Moore, wins the John Deere Breeders' Cup Juvenile Fillies Turf at Keeneland Sun Goddess confirmed herself as a two-year-old out of the ordinary with a clear-cut win Breeders' Cup Juvenile Fillies Turf at Keeneland. Seen by many as the banker of the two-day meeting, she already had three Group Ones in Europe to her credit but she had to contend with the journey to America and stall nine. However, Ryan Moore got her out of the stalls sharply and across to the inside in the perfect position just behind the leader whereas her main market rival, Francis-Henri Graffard's Amusingly, had to settle at the rear of the field. As soon as Moore kicked clear early in the straight the race was over as a contest and once again it was left to Joseph O'Brien's Green Empress to chase her home, the fourth time she has been second to the winner this year. messages.text: Furious Komatsu dismisses 'nonsense' reports of Bearman demanding £5m salary

metadata.summary: Haas boss Ayao Komatsu has furiously dismissed reports claiming that contract extension talks with Oliver Bearman are being held up by the British driver demanding a £5m annual salary.
metadata.content: Oliver Bearman: Haas boss Ayao Komatsu furiously dismisses reports claiming British driver is demanding £5m annual salary | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Oliver Bearman: Haas boss Ayao Komatsu furiously dismisses reports claiming British driver is demanding £5m annual salary Watch every Mexico City GP session live on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 9pm on Saturday and the race at 8pm on Sunday Friday 30 October 2026 21:47, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu has dismissed speculation suggesting Oliver Bearman will be leaving the team Haas boss Ayao Komatsu has furiously dismissed reports claiming that contract extension talks with Oliver Bearman are being held up by the British driver demanding a £5m annual salary. Both Bearman and Komatsu have expressed confidence in recent weeks that a deal will be done to extend the 21-year-old's current contract, which expires at the end of the 2026 season. With Haas having already announced the signing of Bearman's fellow Ferrari junior Rafael Camara to replace Esteban Ocon next season, the lack of confirmation on his own future has led to speculation over what the issues are that are holding up the deal.
